title: Schinzel's Hypothesis H
exact_target: If irreducible integer polynomials have no fixed local obstruction, must they simultaneously take prime values infinitely often?

sources.citation: Federico Scavia, Arithmetic Geometry and Algebraic Groups, Conjecture 3.1 (2026).
On The Schinzel–Wójcik Problem Under Hypothesis H.

Alexei N.\ Skorobogatov and Efthymios Sofos, \emph{Schinzel Hypothesis on average and rational points}, Inventiones Mathematicae 231 (2023), 673--739; arXiv:2005.02998; DOI 10.1007/s00222-022-01153-6. Introduction and Theorems 1.1--1.2.

Tim Browning, Efthymios Sofos and Joni Ter\"av\"ainen, \emph{Bateman--Horn, polynomial Chowla and the Hasse principle with probability 1}, arXiv:2212.10373v2, 21 May 2026, Theorems 1.2 and 1.4 and the introduction.
John Friedlander and Henryk Iwaniec, \emph{Asymptotic sieve for primes}, Annals of Mathematics 148 (1998), 1041--1065; arXiv:math/9811186, Section 1.

Huan Xiao, \emph{From Golomb to Schinzel}, Preprints.org manuscript 202505.0651, version 2, posted 9 June 2025, Section 3, especially the transition from (3.8) to (3.9) and the paragraph following (3.14).
